Welcome to Caroline Haslett Primary School
I would like to wish you a very warm welcome to Caroline Haslett Primary School (CHPS). As Headteacher, I am proud to share with you the wonderful features of our school and the values which underpin everything we do. At Caroline Haslett our motto is: ‘nil satis nisi optimum' (nothing but the best is good enough).
Our school is a happy, ambitious and inclusive school, reflecting the rich diversity of families in our area. Our teaching team is characterised by its dynamic, creative and caring approach. We are always seeking to learn and improve, and we go the extra mile for our pupils to have the opportunity to do the same.

SEN referral for autism and ADHD
SEN referral for autism and ADHD
There is a new referral route for autism and ADHD diagnostic assessments for children and young people called SHINE (Specialist Hub for Integrated Neurodevelopmental Evaluation).
SHINE brings together Community Paediatrics and CAMHS diagnostic assessment services. It is done electronically. Mrs Thomson can complete the referral on your behalf. Please get in touch if you would like further information.
News & Events
Latest News

Clubs
Please contact the school office for further details regarding the clubs we offer at Caroline Haslett Primary School.
For Breakfast Clubs, please bring your child to the school office door, dressed in appropriate clothing, at 7.55am.
After-school clubs will all start straight from school and will finish at 4.30pm (unless otherwise stated).
There may be other school events held that will mean cancelling clubs. If sessions need to be cancelled later on, advance warning will be given and these sessions will be refunded if necessary.
Please only apply for clubs your child definitely wants to join.
Clubs can only run if enough children have signed up and if you withdraw your request, you will still be charged. Once signed up, you are committed for the full term.
If your child participates in an outdoor club, and it is raining, the club will move indoors, where possible, and children will take part in an indoor activity. Please ensure children have appropriate footwear and clothing as the field may be muddy.
Payments are for all sessions, and we regret we are not able to part refund due to absence or participation in team matches. If, for any reason, your child is unable to attend a session, PLEASE let the school office know.
We have an external supplier 'Let's Kick it' that run some of our clubs. Booking and payment for these clubs is done online, directly through them.
The latest clubs are listed in the document below.

pageCache.text:
PE & Sports Premium
In April 2013, the government declared a certain amount of funding for physical education and school sport. Every school, including Caroline Haslett Primary, has received a sum that has, and will continue, to be used to improve the breadth of our provision.
The school is responsible for determining how the funding is best used. We believe, as a school, that this funding will support us improve our physical education and sports provision and help us to further our approach.
Meeting national curriculum requirements for swimming and water safety
What percentage of your current Year 6 cohort swim competently, confidently and proficiently over a distance of at least 25 metres?
What percentage of your current Year 6 cohort use a range of strokes effectively [for example, front crawl, backstroke and breaststroke]?
What percentage of your current Year 6 cohort perform safe self-rescue in different water-based situations?
Schools can choose to use the Primary PE and Sport Premium to provide additional provision for swimming, but this must be for activity over and above the national curriculum requirements. Have you used it in this way?
PE & Sports Premium

Governors
Caroline Haslett School’s Governing Board
The Governing Board works with the headteacher and the staff at the school to make sure that the school provides a good quality of education for all its pupils. Governors work in partnership with the headteacher to set the strategic direction of the school. Governors are not expected and should not make day to day decisions about how the school is run. That is the role of the Headteacher and senior staff.
Governors have three main roles:
Our main role is to promote ongoing improvements in standards throughout the school. We help the Headteacher and staff to plan the school's long-term direction and evaluate progress. We also help to set the aims and values of the school and are responsible for some staff appointments, including the Headteacher.
You may get in touch with the Governing Board via the school office.
Call 01908 231101 or email schooloffice@carolinehaslett.milton-keynes.sch.uk
We meet formally a minimum of three times a year, i.e. once a term. Meeting dates are usually set well in advance and meetings generally last between two and three hours. Governors are expected to be well-prepared for these meetings and attendance is expected, with apologies only for good reasons. In addition to the full governing body, there are two additional committees:
Associate governors have voting rights on the committee on which they sit, but not on the full governing board meetings.

English (Reading including Phonics)
At Caroline Haslett, we believe that reading is the gateway to endless learning and exciting adventures. A love of books opens up new worlds, and we are committed to nurturing this passion in every child. We know that fostering a love of reading is one of the most powerful ways to expand a child’s horizons, and we make it a priority to encourage this from the very start.
We want every child at Caroline Haslett to develop a lifelong love of reading, along with the skills and fluency needed to succeed academically. This is promoted throughout the school via regular library visits, class stories and novels, including our Master Reader books, and a variety of special events such as World Book Day celebrations, book fairs, and other activities designed to make reading fun. We also encourage children to share reading experiences at home. To further support our reading culture, we’ve introduced a new playground library shed, giving children access to books even while outside.
By the time our children leave at the end of Year 6, we want them to read with fluency, confidence, and passion. Our goal is for them to have developed strong reading skills that deepen their understanding, preparing them for success in Key Stage 3 and beyond.
We approach reading instruction with enthusiasm, passion, and a wide range of opportunities to explore different types of texts. We are dedicated to sparking each child’s interest in books, making sure no opportunity is missed. Teachers model reading for pleasure by reading aloud regularly, using high-quality texts to demonstrate the joy of storytelling. They introduce children to a variety of genres, including fiction, non-fiction, poetry, diaries and reports, ensuring that children encounter a rich tapestry of writing. We also aim to reflect our school values through our selection of books, promoting diversity, equality and inclusivity.
In addition to reading, our English curriculum draws clear connections between reading and writing. We encourage children to read like writers and to write with their readers in mind.
Once phonics instruction is complete, all children at Caroline Haslett participate in daily Master Reader sessions with their class teacher. These sessions are designed to help children refine their skills and become confident, capable readers, ready to embark on their next chapter of learning.
English (Reading including Phonics)

English (Writing)
At Caroline Haslett, we strive to ignite a passion for writing in all our children, helping them develop the skills needed to succeed in their education. Our writing curriculum engages children with a variety of stimuli, before focusing on vocabulary, sentence structure, and composition. Children write across a range of fiction and non-fiction styles, with connections made across the curriculum to deepen understanding and meaning.
The curriculum is carefully sequenced with clear progression, revisiting and building on essential skills each year. It runs parallel to our Master Readers, ensuring children see the connection between reading and writing. We teach children to write with purpose, and to read critically as writers, always having the impact of the reader in mind.
In the Early Years and Key Stage 1, we focus on building foundational skills, including handwriting, phonics, and sentence structure. By Key Stage 2, we expand on these skills, strengthening grammar, spelling, and vocabulary. By the end of Year 6, children will have a broad vocabulary and the writing skills needed for success in Key Stage 3 and beyond.

Maths
We love maths at CHPS and follow the Maths Mastery approach. On our page contains information about our calculation policy, overviews of work and information about our daily maths lessons.
At Caroline Haslett Primary School we have adopted a mastery approach to teaching and learning mathematics. We believe that ability within mathematics is not fixed and that all pupils have the potential to achieve. Mastery is not just being able to memorise key facts and procedures. Mastery involves knowing why as well as knowing that and knowing how. It means being able to use knowledge appropriately, flexibly and creatively and to apply it to new and unfamiliar situations.
